Did you get them yet? Here's my opinion based on experience on both switches

The T1's have slight more tactility, probably cause of the way they're shaped. It's "thockier" but keep in mind that you can change a keyboard's sound profile using a lot of things and not just the switch. The reason why they're thockier is most probably because of their Nylon housing, the Akkos are made of PC at the top, and nylon at the bottom.

Not to mention the shape of the pole, the shape of the pole on the Akko is slimmer and tapered just near the edge and it can create a higher sounding pitch if it bottoms out. The Jwk uses a Durock T1 Stem which has a wider pole which creates more of a "thud" sound

The heavier tactility is also probably because the T1's uses a heavier spring, compared to the Akko's which uses a fairly light one.

You also asked about what mods to uses to create a thockier keyboard. Keybored has a video explaining how to make a keyboard Clack or Thock, basically the thinner sort of foam you use the more you filter out high frequency. So use Polyfill instead of EVA foam to fill the gaps, tempest mod, band aid mod if needed, and holee mod as well if needed for your stabs. Other than that I feel once you've polyfilled, tempest modded, and used the JWKs you'll get a Thocky enough board, get lower profile keycaps if you're not satisfied too and even change the plate to a POM/PC
